Class Database

java.lang.Object
Database
public final class Database extends Object
Database access shared by both GUIs: the connection settings from .env, transactions, new ids, the latest order date, and the inventory items that are not used exactly as a recipe says.
Author:
Brian Fu

  • Method Details

    • connect

      public static Connection connect() throws SQLException
      Opens a connection using the DB_HOST, DB_NAME, DB_USER and DB_PASSWORD settings read by getSetting(String).
      Returns:
      an open connection to the team database
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the database cannot be reached or the login is rejected
      IllegalStateException - if any of the four settings is missing

    • getSetting

      public static String getSetting(String key)
      Returns a setting such as DB_PASSWORD from an environment variable if one is set, otherwise from the .env file in the folder the program is run from (the repository root). Blank lines and # comments in the file are skipped, a leading export is allowed, and surrounding quotes are removed from the value.
      Parameters:
      key - the name of the setting, such as "DB_HOST"
      Returns:
      the value of the setting, without surrounding quotes
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the setting is missing or the .env file cannot be read

    • runInTransaction

      public static void runInTransaction(Connection connection, Database.TransactionWork work) throws SQLException
      Runs the work as one transaction: commits if it succeeds, rolls back and rethrows if it fails. Auto-commit is turned off for the duration and restored afterwards, whatever happens.
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection to run the transaction on
      work - the database changes to make together
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the work or the commit fails; nothing is saved in that case
      See Also:
      • lockAndGetNextId(Connection, String)

    • lockAndGetNextId

      public static int lockAndGetNextId(Connection connection, String tableName) throws SQLException
      Locks a table and returns its next free id. Call it inside runInTransaction(Connection, TransactionWork) so the lock lasts until the commit and two users cannot be given the same id.
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection the transaction is running on
      tableName - the table to lock, quoted if needed, such as "\"Order\""
      Returns:
      one more than the largest id in the table, or 1 if it is empty
      Throws:
      SQLException - if the table cannot be locked or read

    • latestOrderDate

      public static LocalDate latestOrderDate(Connection connection, boolean salesOnly)
      Returns the date of the most recent order, or today if there are none, so reports open on recent data.
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection to read from
      salesOnly - true to look only at sales, false to include returns, voids and discards
      Returns:
      the date of the latest matching order, or today if the query fails or finds nothing
